title: PyTorch ONNX exporter produces invalid Gemm node
body:
Hello everyone,

I am not familiar with onnx. I have exported a model from torch to onnx, the torch model works fine, but the when I try to do inference with the onnx file, I got the following error message.

```
[ShapeInferenceError] All inputs to Concat must have same rank. Input 1 has rank 0 != 1
```
How could I solve this error?

Thank you so much

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: This is saying the input is a scalar and should have been a vector instead. `Rank==len(shape of tensor)`. How did you export your model? Please test with `torch.onnx.export(..., dynamo=True, report=True)` using the latest torch-nightly. Attach the generated report if there is an error. Thanks!

comments.body:
The error is this: In `# File: /home/<user>/rtgrouppose/src/models/rtgrouppose_/fdr_transformer.py:139 in forward, code: x = F.linear(x, project.to(x.device)).reshape(-1, 4)`, you called `linear` on `x` and `project`. Since `project` has shape `[33]`, and ONNX requires both tensors to be 2d (https://onnx.ai/onnx/operators/onnx__Gemm.html#inputs), an error is raised.

The fix would be either:

1. update your code in `fdr_transformer.py:139` to use matmul instead of linear.
2. update your code in `fdr_transformer.py:139` to reshape the project tensor to 2d before calling linear
3. ~update onnxscript aten_linear implementation to accept a 1d input.~ According to documentation weight is always 2d: https://<redacted-host>/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Linear.html, nevertheless https://github.com/microsoft/onnxscript/pull/2340

## Here is how you can locate the error

(1) See error message `onnxruntime.capi.onnxruntime_pybind11_state.Fail: [ONNXRuntimeError] : 1 : FAIL : Node (node_Gemm_3722) Op (Gemm) [ShapeInferenceError] Second input does not have rank 2`

(2) In the report, locate `node_Gemm_3722` in the ONNX model.

```
    3721 |  # node_Cast_3721
            %"_to_copy_1"<FLOAT,[33]> ⬅️ ::Cast(%"cat_14") {to=FLOAT}

            %"linear_32"<FLOAT,[2040*s0]> ⬅️ ::Gemm(%"softmax_4", %"_to_copy_1") {beta=1.0, transB=True, alpha=1.0, transA=0}
    3723 |  # node_Constant_3723
            %"val_2071"<?,?> ⬅️ ::Constant() {value=Tensor<INT64,[2]>(array([-1,  4]), name=None)}
```

```py

            view_378: "f32[510*s0, 4]" = torch.ops.aten.view.default(linear_32, [-1, 4]);  linear_32 = None
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
```
    9391 |  # node_Div_9391
            %"val_6553"<?,?> ⬅️ ::Div(%"getitem_149", %"val_840")
    9392 |  # node_Floor_9392
            %"floor_divide"<INT64,[s0,60]> ⬅️ ::Floor(%"val_6553")
    9393 |  # node_Mod_9393
            %"label"<INT64,[s0,60]> ⬅️ ::Mod(%"getitem_149", %"val_840") {fmod=0}
```

ONNX doesn't define the floor operation on int64 inputs.  This op was generated from `floor_divide`:

```
             # File: <eval_with_key>.14:7 in forward, code: topk_1 = torch.ops.aten.topk.default(view_102, 60, 1);  view_102 = None
            topk_1 = torch.ops.aten.topk.default(view_601, 60, 1);  view_601 = None
            getitem_148: "f32[s0, 60]" = topk_1[0]
            getitem_149: "i64[s0, 60]" = topk_1[1];  topk_1 = None
            
             # File: <eval_with_key>.14:10 in forward, code: floor_divide = torch.ops.aten.floor_divide.default(getitem_70, 2)
            floor_divide: "i64[s0, 60]" = torch.ops.aten.floor_divide.default(getitem_149, 2)
            
             # File: <eval_with_key>.14:11 in forward, code: remainder = torch.ops.aten.remainder.Scalar(getitem_70, 2);  getitem_70 = None
            remainder: "i64[s0, 60]" = torch.ops.aten.remainder.Scalar(getitem_149, 2);  getitem_149 = None
            
```

If you have access to this part of the source code, you can cast the second output of topk to float32 first. I will separately see how I can fix this bug. Thanks for helping improve the onnx exporter. (https://github.com/microsoft/onnxscript/pull/2343)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: You can read more about the api here https://<redacted-host>/docs/main/onnx_dynamo.html#api-reference. Set `external_data=False` to store data inside the onnx file (otherwise the weights are stored in a separate file), you should get a file with comparable size. `dynamo=True` is the recommended new path for exporting onnx models.
